card.name: Lab test words and mid-drug-name pieces
card.fires_on: Lab-test nouns such as assay or tests in warnings about test interference, and partway through drug names like levonorgestrel, triazolam, EOVIST and contraindicated. It also fires on words that start a general condition clause.

modes.label: Lab test wording
modes.description: The word assay or tests in a note that a lab method may give wrong results.
modes.example: Do not screen patients who have received WASKYRA ® for HIV infection using a PCR-based<< assay>>.

modes.label: Inside drug names
modes.description: Partway through a drug or brand name or a long medical word.
modes.example: Use of perampanel with contraceptives containing<< lev>>onorgestrel may render them less

modes.label: Scope words in a clause
modes.description: A word that opens a general 'any situation or period' condition.
modes.example: in any situation of stress occurring during that<< period>> of discontinuation, corticosteroid

card.writes: It seems to promote words meaning 'anywhere' or 'whenever' (including Chinese equivalents), adding a sense of any case that fits the condition.
card.plain: It marks lab-test words and parts of drug names in warnings, where a general rule about any case is likely to follow.
